[internet-national-regional] DETAILED tier (57 entries, all links fetched this session via curl, the Zendesk Help Center API, WebFetch or a headless browser for JS/Cloudflare-protected sites): every national ISP and every U.S. cable/telco ISP with roughly 100k+ broadband customers - Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox (now joining Spectrum), Optimum/Suddenlink, AT&T (Fiber/Internet Air), Verizon (Fios/5G Home/LTE Home), Frontier (now Verizon), CenturyLink, Quantum Fiber (now AT&T), Brightspeed, Kinetic/Windstream, TDS, Ziply (BCE), Consolidated/Fidium, altafiber, Hawaiian Telcom, Mediacom, Sparklight/Cable One (incl. Hargray), Astound (RCN/Wave/Grande/enTouch), WOW!, Breezeline, Midco, Armstrong, Service Electric, Blue Ridge, Buckeye, MaxxSouth, Shentel/Glo Fiber, Lumos, Metronet, Google Fiber, GCI, Alaska Communications, Sonic, EarthLink, Liberty PR, Claro PR; fixed wireless (T-Mobile Home Internet, Verizon 5G Home and AT&T Internet Air within their carrier entries, Starry, Rise, Nextlink, Wisper); satellite (Starlink, HughesNet, Viasat); fiber overbuilders (ALLO, GoNetspeed, Greenlight, Omni, Ripple, Wyyerd, Bluepeak, UTOPIA open-access fee, Conexon Connect); and the federal Lifeline program. Each detailed entry records low-cost/senior programs found (e.g., Xfinity Internet Essentials, Spectrum/Cox Internet Assist $15 incl. SSI recipients, Optimum Advantage, AT&T Access, Verizon Forward, Mediacom Seniors Connect (65+), Buckeye/MaxxSouth Senior Living Pak, Astound senior discount, Liberty PR Medicare Advantage card payments). Several billers have built-in/mandatory autopay (Google Fiber, Starlink, Viasat, Quantum Fiber, Greenlight, Starry, Sonic, EarthLink new plans) - noted per entry. ROSTER tier (~306 entries): generated programmatically from the FCC Form 477 (June 2021) holding-company provider table (rosters/telecom_providers.csv): ALL cable holding companies, all satellite providers, fiber/competitive ISPs covering 150k+ people, fixed-wireless ISPs covering 750k+ people or 4+ states, and copper/DSL non-ILEC holding companies covering 750k+ people; plus ACA Connects/NCTA members not matched in FCC data, plus 15 hand-added post-2021 entrants/rebrands (Ezee Fiber, i3, Point Broadband, IdeaTek, Docomo Pacific, HBC, MCTV, Lightcurve, XMission, WEHCO, Blue Stream, Summit, Surf, Ting, Viya). Holding companies already covered by a detailed entry are omitted from the roster, and names already present in internet-rural-coops.json are skipped to avoid duplication. COMPLETENESS: checked against the FCC Form 477 provider list (every fixed-broadband provider nationally as of 2021) - every holding company with >2M people covered is either detailed here or is a small single-market WISP/rural telco covered by internet-rural-coops or landline-telcos. Long-tail rural telcos, telephone/electric co-op fiber, municipal fiber (EPB, UTOPIA member cities, etc.) and ~2,000 small WISPs are intentionally in internet-rural-coops.json; ILEC landline billing in landline-telcos.json; TV-only billing in cable-satellite-tv.json. KNOWN GAPS / NEXT PASS: (1) FCC Form 477 data is from 2021 - refresh the roster from the FCC National Broadband Map BDC provider list (broadbandmap.fcc.gov data download; blocked to automated fetch this session) to catch 2022-2026 entrants and mergers (e.g., Charter-Cox, Verizon-Frontier, AT&T-Lumen fiber, T-Mobile JV purchases of Metronet/Lumos, BCE-Ziply, T-Mobile-UScellular). (2) Roster entries lack websites/phones for most holding companies (FCC data has no URLs). (3) Mediacom's Answer Center and HughesNet FAQ Center are login/JS apps without public article URLs, so only T&C/FAQ-hub links are recorded; Cox and Optimum customer-service numbers are location-specific. (4) Mailing payment addresses not published online for Xfinity, Spectrum, AT&T, Verizon, WOW, Mediacom, Breezeline, Consolidated (printed on bill). (5) Customer counts are approximate (company reports) and null where unknown. (6) Starlink/Viasat/HughesNet low-income programs not found; Amazon Kuiper/Leo consumer service not yet researched. REVIEWER PASS (2026-09-29): (a) Link check - every URL in all detailed entries (334 unique URLs incl. website/login/help) was requested with curl this session: 307 returned 200, 23 returned 403 bot-blocks (Sonic, Starry, Blue Ridge, Liberty PR Zendesk/sites - previously verified via browser), 3 timeouts (lifelinesupport.org). Redirected canonical URLs fixed for Breezeline help articles and WOW billing help. Some statements_history links (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Optimum) are sign-in pages, not public articles. (b) De-duplication - merged 10 duplicate records (Greenlight, ALLO, Docomo Pacific, Blue Stream, Ting, Viya x2, i3 Broadband, TruVista, Tongue River) and removed 52 municipal/co-op/small-WISP roster records that duplicate entries already in internet-rural-coops.json (e.g., EPB, OzarksGo, CDE Lightband, BTES, Frankfort Plant Board, Murray, Glasgow EPB). (c) Upgrades/additions - upgraded Hotwire Communications (Fision; in scope and important for Florida 55+ communities), Blue Stream Fiber, i3 Broadband, Lightcurve, Docomo Pacific and Ezee Fiber to detailed; added Vexus Fiber (now Metronet/T-Mobile Fiber), PCs for People (low-cost prepaid internet, detailed) and roster entries for Amazon Leo (satellite) and Human-I-T. Armstrong paperless link corrected. (d) Still gaps: web search budget was exhausted during this pass, so discovery relied on direct site fetches; Ting (Radware CAPTCHA), Summit Broadband and Viya (unreachable) remain roster-only; Hotwire and Docomo publish no public autopay/statement how-to pages; the FCC 2021 roster was not refreshed from the BDC provider list; EveryoneOn (offer locator, not a biller) not added. A website was accepted only when the fetched page title/body named the provider (or a redirect from the provider's own legacy domain proved an acquisition/rebrand); parked, for-sale, expired, hijacked and same-name-unrelated domains were rejected and noted. entries.name: Lifeline (federal phone/internet discount program, USAC)
entries.parent_company: Federal Communications Commission / Universal Service Administrative Company (USAC)
entries.service_area_detail: Nationwide program; discount applied by a participating provider on the customer's monthly bill
entries.phone_customer_service: Lifeline Support Center (800) 234-9473 (7 days, 9am-9pm ET; LifelineSupport@usac.org)
entries.senior_programs: Up to $9.25/month off phone, internet or bundle (up to $34.25 on Tribal lands) for households in SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing, Veterans Pension/Survivors Benefit or at/below 135% of federal poverty guidelines. Many seniors on Medicaid/SSI qualify. Apply via National Verifier (getinternet.gov); OR and TX use state processes; CA has separate CA LifeLine. Annual recertification: https://www.lifelinesupport.org/recertify/. Find participating companies: https://www.lifelinesupport.org/companies-near-me/.
entries.notes: Not a biller - a discount on the ISP/phone bill. The Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP, $30/mo) ended in June 2024 for lack of funding; ISP low-cost plans (Xfinity Internet Essentials, Spectrum/Cox Internet Assist, Optimum Advantage, AT&T Access, Verizon Forward, etc.) are listed on each ISP entry. lifelinesupport.org fetched via WebFetch this session (curl blocked).
